questions.q: In self-attention, what does the 'score' between two tokens measure?
options: How aligned their vector representations are, computed as a dot product
The alphabetical distance between the two words
Which token was typed first by the user
The number of letters each token has
questions.explain: The attention score is a dot product between a query vector and each token's vector — a measure of how aligned (similar in direction) the two vectors are.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, why did 'sat' end up attending mostly to itself (about 58%) but still pull about 21% from 'The' and 21% from 'cat'?
options: Those were the raw, un-normalized dot product scores directly
The order the tokens appeared in the sentence
A random number generator
Softmax turned the raw scores into weights that sum to 1, and sat's self-score was highest but not the only nonzero one
questions.explain: Softmax converts raw dot-product scores into a probability-like distribution — the highest score gets the most weight, but every nonzero score still contributes some.

questions.q: Why does self-attention remove the RNN's long-range bottleneck from lesson 20?
options: It uses a bigger hidden state than RNNs do
It processes tokens in alphabetical order
Every token's score against every other token is a direct calculation, not something relayed through a chain of intermediate steps
It eliminates the need for any numerical computation
questions.explain: Because attention scores are direct dot products between any two tokens, a relationship between distant tokens is exactly as direct as one between adjacent tokens — no information has to survive a long relay.

questions.q: Why did self-attention's parallelism matter as much as the attention mechanism itself?
options: It made transformers require less training data
It removed the need for a loss function
It made the models smaller
Because no token's calculation depends on another's finishing first, all of them can run at the same time on hardware built for parallel computation — making much larger-scale training feasible
questions.explain: Independence between tokens' attention calculations is what let transformers be trained efficiently on GPUs at a scale RNNs' step-by-step design couldn't match.

questions.q: What problem does positional encoding solve in a transformer?
options: It makes attention scores sum to exactly 1
Dot products alone don't encode token order, so positional encoding adds information about each token's position back into its vector
It replaces the need for an activation function
It converts text into images for a CNN
questions.explain: Dot-product attention is order-blind on its own; positional encoding is added explicitly so word order (e.g. 'dog bites man' vs. 'man bites dog') still affects the result.
